content: Inline some optional imports that are only used for certain CLI commands. [#4606](https://github.com/pallets/flask/pull/4606)

github.content:
### GitHub Pull Request #4606 inline conditional imports for cli behaviors
`dotenv`, `ssl`, and `importlib_metadata` are only used in certain parts when running `flask` CLI commands. Don't import them at the top level. This also makes type checking a bit easier, since mypy doesn't like conditional imports.

### GitHub Issue #4600 callback types should use `bound` type vars instead of base types
* Flask 2.1.2
* Python 3.9.12
* mypy 0.950 (tested also 0.910)

For this type definition on `after_request`:

https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/bd56d19b167822a9a23e2e9e2a07ccccc36baa8d/src/flask/typing.py#L39

It generates this mypy error:

```
error: Argument 1 to "after_request" of "Scaffold" has incompatible type "Callable[[Arg(Response, 'response')], Response]"; expected "Callable[[Response], Response]"
```

For the sample code of:

```python3
from flask import Flask, Response

def my_func(response: Response) -> Response:
    print("my after request func")
    return response

app = Flask(__name__)
app.after_request(my_func)  # <-- type error
```

This code works just fine, and did not generate typing errors for Flask 2.0.2

content: `instance_path` for namespace packages uses the path closest to the imported submodule. [#4610](https://github.com/pallets/flask/issues/4610)

github.content:
### GitHub Pull Request #4610 find instance_path for namespace package
Fix `Flask.auto_find_instance_path()` so that it handles correctly namespace packages residing in several different locations, e.g. from several projects installed in development mode.

Return not the first submodule search location but the one most close to Flask app import name.

- fixes #4602
